A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 22-page versions of VideoJAM, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F. Corresponding content can be matched despite reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original motion-sensitivity experiments, video-generation comparisons, human evaluations and ablations in Sections 3 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds results comparing VideoJAM-30B with DiT-30B on native VBench prompts in Table 6.

M1.justification: Joint appearance-motion prediction and Inner-Guidance remain unchanged. Section 4.3 newly explains appearance-only loss when optical flow is dropped, presenting this as clarification of existing training rather than an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: V2 additionally evaluates native VBench prompts (Appendix D, Table 6); v1 uses VBench metrics only on VideoJAM-bench and Movie Gen prompts. The training data, original benchmarks and all 128 VideoJAM-bench prompts are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the VideoJAM-bench, Movie Gen and ablation comparisons. The added VBench evaluation uses the already evaluated DiT-30B base model without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: New Table 6 evaluates ten additional VBench dimensions, including object class, multiple objects, color, spatial relationships, scene and style, using native VBench prompts. Existing training settings, resolution, sampling and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The frame-permutation and SDEdit motivation experiments, guidance and optical-flow ablations, and failure examples are retained. New Table 6 supplies additional benchmark scores rather than a new ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions specify one run per model with the same random seed across benchmark prompts and five raters per human comparison. V2 adds no repeated-run analysis, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports ten comparisons: VideoJAM improves eight metrics, ties temporal flickering and scores lower on scene (49.7 versus DiT-30B's 52.1). Table 3's VideoJAM-4B appearance score changes from 74.9 to 75.1, matching Table 1. Other matched results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A, Equation 11 expands the log-gradient of the existing probability product into separate terms. This is an algebraic clarification of Equation 10; the assumptions, argument and resulting guidance formulation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about pixel objectives, joint appearance-motion representations, Inner-Guidance, improved motion coherence and complementary visual quality. Added evaluation supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the training objective and motion guidance are retained, as are limitations concerning small or distant moving objects and complex physical interactions. The added VBench discussion reiterates the existing interpretation that motion improvements can coexist with visual quality.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies that dropping optical flow during training makes the loss appearance-only. This supplies useful implementation detail. Appendix C's hardware, training budgets, architecture and inference settings remain unchanged; the existing project URL is merely relocated.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MotionCraft, MoCoGAN, Video-LaVIT, HyperHuman and Shen et al.'s content-motion decoupling work, while removing several references including Emu Edit, DynamiCrafter and I2VGen-XL. This locally broadens discussion of motion separation and structural or physical priors without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: V2 converts experiment labels into numbered subsections 5.1–5.4, makes localized explanatory and related-work edits, and adds conference publication information. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 6, renumbers the retained Movie Gen tables from 6–7 to 7–8, and adjusts table spacing and emphasis. The project link and surrounding text are repositioned. Existing figures and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens validation through additional VBench comparisons, clarifies loss handling during optical-flow dropout and resolves Table 3's inconsistency with Table 1. These improve evidence coverage, reproducibility and clarity. The gains are limited because the central method, principal findings and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
